question: A maternity claim has been submitted under the Oriental Happy Family Floater Policy. How long must the policy have been continuously in force before maternity expenses are payable?
ground_truth: Maternity expenses are covered only after the policy has been continuously in force for 24 months (under the Diamond Plan).

question: A claim under the Star Health Arogya Sanjeevani policy cites a pre-existing condition. What waiting period must be served before that claim is payable?
ground_truth: Pre-existing diseases are covered after a waiting period of 48 months (4 years) of continuous coverage from the policy's inception date, provided they were declared at the time of application and accepted by the insurer.

question: A claim for robotic surgery has been submitted under the Navi Health Super Top Up policy. Is that procedure payable as a modern treatment method?
ground_truth: Yes, robotic surgeries are listed among the covered Modern Treatment Methods, along with stereotactic radiosurgery, bronchial thermoplasty, and stem cell therapy, wherever medically indicated.

question: A claim under Star Health Arogya Sanjeevani is for inpatient AYUSH treatment (Ayurveda, Yoga, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Homeopathy). Is it payable, and up to what limit?
ground_truth: Yes, inpatient care treatment under AYUSH systems of medicine is covered up to the sum insured limit specified in the policy schedule, at any AYUSH hospital.

question: A claim for cosmetic surgery has been submitted under the New India Top-Up Mediclaim Policy. Is it excluded from cover?
ground_truth: No, change of life or cosmetic/aesthetic treatment of any description is excluded, along with plastic surgery not necessitated by an accident or illness.

question: A claim under the Star Health Senior Citizens Red Carpet policy is for an injury sustained during hazardous or adventure sports. Is it payable?
ground_truth: No, expenses for treatment necessitated by participation as a professional in hazardous or adventure sports -- such as para-jumping, rock climbing, mountaineering, or scuba diving -- are excluded under Code Excl 09.

question: When calculating the payable amount on a hospitalisation claim under the Star Health Arogya Sanjeevani policy, what room rent and ICU limits apply?
ground_truth: Room rent, boarding, and nursing expenses are limited to 2% of the sum insured, subject to a maximum of Rs 5,000 per day; ICU/ICCU charges are limited to 5% of the sum insured, subject to a maximum of Rs 10,000 per day.

question: A cataract surgery claim has been submitted under the Star Health Arogya Sanjeevani policy. What sub-limit caps the payable amount?
ground_truth: Cataract treatment is subject to a sub-limit of 25% of the sum insured or Rs 40,000 per eye per policy year, whichever is lower.

question: A hospitalisation claim has been submitted under the Star Health Arogya Sanjeevani policy. What co-payment does the policyholder bear on the admissible claim amount?
ground_truth: Every admissible claim under the Arogya Sanjeevani policy carries a co-payment of 5% of the admissible claim amount, which the policyholder bears; the insurer pays the balance.

question: A claim has been submitted under the New India Top-Up Mediclaim policy. How does the deductible determine what this policy pays?
ground_truth: The Top-Up Mediclaim policy pays only the portion of admissible hospitalisation expenses that exceeds the deductible chosen and recorded on the policy schedule. Expenses up to that deductible are borne by the insured or met by an underlying policy; the wording does not fix a single deductible figure, since the amount is an option selected at inception.
